controls.name: T2b-decline
controls.why: an EARLIER accepted mover (id 3, sorted first on descending id) has already reserved (1,0) — m's own cell — as its landing, so the exchange would create a contested landing the engine would break on id. alpha must decline.

controls.name: T2b-fire-twin
controls.why: the same board with the earlier mover sent the other way, so (1,0) is NOT reserved. One fact changed; alpha must now fire. This is what makes the decline above evidence about T2b rather than about an inert alpha.

controls.name: T2-decline-speed
controls.why: m has movement_speed 2, so its landing (3,0) is two cells from its own cell (1,0); U at (3,0) has speed 1 and cannot reach (1,0) in one tick. A bare adjacency test would wave this through; next_cell rejects it.

controls.name: T2-fire-twin-speed
controls.why: the same board with U's speed raised to 2, which makes the exchange a legal single tick for U. Also the T4(a) demonstration: a detour DOES exist here ((2,0) is free), and the ruled construction swaps anyway because U is idle.

controls.name: T3-partner-forbidden-decline
controls.why: m.cell (1,0) is forbidden to non-priority units and U (id 1) is not a priority id, so the exchange would push U into a door cell it is forbidden to enter. The base never had to ask this because U was not moving; alpha makes it move, so alpha owes the check.

controls.name: T3-partner-forbidden-fire-twin
controls.why: the same board with U also a priority id, which is exactly the fact the clause tests. alpha fires.

controls.name: positional-map-count-mismatch
controls.why: three own units, two commands: the one-command-per-unit invariant does not hold, so a positional map cannot be trusted and alpha disables itself for the tick. The board is otherwise the firing board.

controls.name: positional-map-id-mismatch
controls.why: the command count matches but a MOVE names an id that is not the positionally-derived one (slot 1 belongs to id 2 and carries `MOVE 4 …`), so the map disagrees with the ids alpha can actually read and alpha disables itself. A cure that rewrites the wrong troll's command is worse than no cure.

controls.name: T1-enemy-blocker
controls.why: the blocker on the landing cell is an ENEMY unit. Enemies may share our cell, so they are never in `reserved` and the branch is not even reached — recorded as a control so the claim is measured rather than asserted.

controls.name: T4b-no-detour-working-partner
controls.why: U is CHOPping, not idle, and m sits in a DEAD END at (0,0) with no detour. the OSC-005/027 shape: the exchange is the only resolution, and U's chop is displaced for the tick.

controls.name: T4-working-partner-with-detour
controls.why: U is working (not idle) and a detour DOES exist (the dead end at (0,0) is widened by (0,1)). Neither T4 clause holds, so alpha must decline and the base's detour must stand. This is the boundary of the one declared behaviour change.
